settings.title: Settings
lens.wide.note: The usual field of view. The phone has to be held higher above the table for the whole pile to fit into the square.
lens.ultra_wide.note: Sees much more of the table at the same height. The card covers fewer pixels, so the camera records at a higher resolution to leave the model the same detail.
rule.run.note: A card is counted when it lies on top in that many frames in a row. A single frame that differs resets the count.
rule.majority.note: A card is counted when it holds the majority of the last frames and no other card appears in them more than once. Single dropouts no longer break the count, but a misreading during a movement now needs a real majority instead of three frames that happen to be neighbours.
settings.feedback_note.ios: For every counted card. All the way left is off. The sound follows the media volume, also in silent mode, and lets music that is playing go on. The iPhone's system haptics still apply.
settings.feedback_note.android: For every counted card. All the way left is off. The sound follows the media volume, also in silent mode, and lets music that is playing go on. The phone's vibration settings still apply.

about.title: About
about.licence_text: JassCardEye is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License 3.0. Distribution through the App Store and Google Play is covered by an additional permission, described in the licence file.
about.model_text: The recognition model was trained with Ultralytics YOLO11 (AGPL-3.0) on one French and one Swiss German Jass deck.
about.credits_note: The suit marks come from Wikimedia Commons and are used unchanged.
about.privacy_text: The app collects no data. The camera images are analysed on the device and not stored; the app has no internet connection, no account and no ads. Only your settings stay on the device.
about.libraries_text.ios: Apart from Apple's frameworks, the app uses no third-party libraries.
about.libraries_text.android: The app uses AndroidX with Jetpack Compose and CameraX, LiteRT by Google and the Kotlin standard library, all under the Apache License 2.0.
